items.title: 台幣逼近32.5元還會貶？外銀看好強勁出口支撐 年底反攻31.5元
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Near 32.5 per Dollar – Will It Depreciate Further? Foreign Banks See Strong Export Support, Expect a Rebound to 31.5 by Year‑End
paras: 分析師表示，全球市場對人工智慧（AI）交易的疑慮引發新台幣走弱，卻掩蓋了台灣經濟的基本韌性；穩健的經濟基本面可望支撐新台幣在年底前回升。
儘管新台幣近期承受沉重壓力，華僑銀行與荷蘭國際集團（ING）仍預期，新台幣將分別回升至兌1美元31.60元與31.50元，較目前水準升值約2%。
這些預測的依據，是台灣強勁的經濟成長與經常帳順差。儘管市場對AI股高估值的疑慮持續推動資金外流，短期壓抑匯率，分析師預期，未來幾個月貿易基本面的支撐終將占上風。
三菱日聯銀行（MUFG）亞洲全球市場研究主管Lin Li表示：「創紀錄的貿易順差與AI相關出口，持續為新台幣提供基本支撐。但外資證券投資流出、對外投資，以及美元與新台幣之間龐大的利差，目前正創造美元需求，抵銷這些支撐。」
她預期，新台幣年底前將升至兌1美元31.8元，並在2027年6月底進一步升至30.9元。
出口與順差強勁 外資撤出台股形成拉鋸
受全球先進晶片需求空前強勁帶動，台灣經常帳順差在2025年底達到近700億美元的歷史新高，近幾個月則溫和收窄。同時，政府將全年經濟成長率預測上修至逾10%，台灣可望迎來2010年以來首次雙位數成長。
不過，這些基本面優勢正與外資撤離潮相互拉鋸。外資周四賣超台股新台幣3,026億元（約93億美元），創單日新高，推動新台幣逼近今年以來兌1美元約32.50元的低點。
雖然分析師不認為這個價位是央行必須捍衛的防線，但仍密切關注，視其為央行可接受匯率區間的重要參考。
ING大中華區首席經濟學家宋林表示：「央行將試圖讓新台幣維持相對區間震盪。我不認為存在必須守住的明確防線，但今年以來，31.5至32.5元似乎一直是央行可以接受的區間。」
道富銀行亞太區總體策略師Jiuk Choi認為，央行更可能著重降低匯率波動，而非鎖定特定價位。他表示：「話雖如此，我們認為美元兌新台幣32.4至32.5元是重要區間，因為這是2026年以來的高點。」
油價與利差添壓力 中期仍看升
除了科技業疑慮，台灣作為能源進口國，偏高的原油價格也為新台幣增添壓力。此外，美國10年期公債殖利率較台灣同天期公債高出約300個基點，具吸引力的利差持續支撐美元普遍走強，壓抑區域貨幣表現。
LGT私人銀行外匯與利率專家Trang Le表示：「短期逆風包括外資撤出台股，以及聯準會立場偏鷹帶動美元走強。」
她指出：「即便如此，強勁的出口動能、穩健的對外收支，以及AI驅動的半導體景氣循環，仍使新台幣中期走勢偏向升值。我們預期，匯率波動將是主軸，而非持續走弱。」
科技財報成下一個匯率關鍵
匯市交易員正關注主要半導體製造商的財報，策略師視其為牽動跨境股市資金流向與匯率波動的下一個關鍵因素。台積電周四公布優於預期的營收展望，卻未能完全平息市場對整體AI基礎建設擴張的疑慮。
道富銀行的Choi表示：「接下來公布的全球科技業財報，可能加劇新台幣波動，尤其市場對AI相關資本支出、獲利能力及中國競爭的敏感度已升高。」
他認為，AI交易疑慮仍可能讓新台幣短期進一步走弱，但預期年底前將回升至兌1美元31.80元。
他表示：「我們認為，新台幣是對沖美元走強的最佳貨幣之一，因為資本與經常帳資金流仍然強勁，而且新台幣也是新興市場中波動率最低的貨幣之一。」
paras_en: Analysts say that global concerns over artificial‑intelligence (AI) trading have weakened the New Taiwan dollar, but this masks the underlying resilience of Taiwan’s economy; a solid economic foundation is expected to support a rebound of the currency before year‑end.

Even though the New Taiwan dollar has been under heavy pressure recently, both OCBC and ING forecast that it will recover to about NT$31.60 per US$1 and NT$31.50 per US$1 respectively, roughly a 2% appreciation from current levels.

These forecasts are based on Taiwan’s strong economic growth and current‑account surplus. Although market worries about over‑valued AI stocks continue to drive capital outflows and suppress the exchange rate in the short term, analysts expect the trade fundamentals to ultimately prevail in the coming months.

Lin Li, head of Asian Global Markets Research at MUFG, said: “Record‑high trade surpluses and AI‑related exports continuously provide fundamental support for the New Taiwan dollar. Yet foreign‑security outflows, outbound investment and the huge interest‑rate differential between the dollar and the New Taiwan dollar are currently creating dollar demand that offsets those supports.”
She projects the New Taiwan dollar will rise to NT$31.8 per US$1 by year‑end and further to NT$30.9 by the end of June 2027.
Strong exports and surplus, foreign‑capital pull‑out creates a tug‑of‑war in Taiwan equities

Fueled by unprecedented demand for advanced chips worldwide, Taiwan’s current‑account surplus is set to hit a historic high of nearly US$70 billion by the end of 2025, though it has narrowed modestly in recent months. At the same time, the government has lifted its full‑year growth forecast to above 10%, positioning Taiwan for its first double‑digit expansion since 2010.

However, these fundamental strengths are being contested by a wave of foreign‑capital outflows. On Thursday foreign investors sold NT$3,026 billion (about US$9.3 billion) of Taiwan equities, a single‑day record, pushing the New Taiwan dollar toward this year’s low of roughly NT$32.50 per US$1.
While analysts do not view this level as a hard floor the central bank must defend, they are watching it closely as an important reference for the exchange‑rate band the bank may tolerate.

Song Lin, chief economist for Greater China at ING, said: “The central bank will try to keep the New Taiwan dollar within a relative range. I don’t see a clear floor that must be defended, but since the start of the year the NT$31.5‑NT$32.5 band has seemed acceptable to the central bank.”

Jiuk Choi, global‑strategy head for Asia‑Pacific at State Street, believes the central bank is more likely to focus on reducing volatility rather than anchoring a specific level. He added: “That said, we see NT$32.4‑NT$32.5 per US$1 as a key zone because it marks the high point reached in 2026.”
Oil prices and interest‑rate spreads add pressure; medium‑term outlook still upward

Beyond tech‑sector concerns, Taiwan’s status as an energy‑importing nation means high crude‑oil prices add further pressure on the New Taiwan dollar. In addition, the U.S. 10‑year Treasury yield is about 300 basis points higher than Taiwan’s comparable bond, and the attractive spread continues to underpin a broadly strong dollar, suppressing regional currencies.
Trang Le, FX and rates specialist at LGT Private Bank, said: “Short‑term headwinds include foreign‑capital outflows from Taiwan equities and a hawkish Fed stance that is bolstering the dollar.”

She noted: “Even so, strong export momentum, solid external balances and an AI‑driven semiconductor cycle still tilt the medium‑term New Taiwan dollar trend toward appreciation. We expect exchange‑rate volatility to be the main driver, not a continued weakening.”
Tech earnings become the next exchange‑rate catalyst

FX traders are watching earnings reports from major semiconductor manufacturers, which strategists see as the next key factor influencing cross‑border equity flows and currency moves. TSMC’s Thursday earnings outlook beat expectations, but did not fully allay market concerns about the broader AI‑infrastructure expansion.

State Street’s Choi said: “The upcoming global tech earnings season could amplify New Taiwan dollar volatility, especially as market sensitivity to AI‑related capex, profitability and competition from China has risen.”
He believes AI‑trading worries could still push the New Taiwan dollar lower in the short term, but expects a rebound to NT$31.80 per US$1 by year‑end.

He added: “We see the New Taiwan dollar as one of the best hedges against a strong dollar because capital and current‑account flows remain robust, and the New Taiwan dollar is also among the least volatile currencies in emerging markets.”

items.title: 美烏矛盾與法國騷亂推升美元！歐元兌多數G10貨幣走貶 今早兌美元一度大跌0.5%
items.title_en: US-Ukraine Tensions and French Unrest Boost the Dollar! Euro Falls Against Most G10 Currencies, Briefly Dropping 0.5% Against the Dollar This Morning
paras: 受美烏矛盾進一步升高及法國大規模抗議活動影響，市場對歐元信心受挫，歐元兌多數G10貨幣在今(19)日亞洲早盤交易時段走低。
周末期間，法國多個城市抗議活動演變為警方與示威者之間的衝突，爆發法國多年來最嚴重的街頭暴力事件，出現搶劫、地標建築遭縱火情況。歐洲多國接連發生示威活動，法國的抗議規模最大，比利時、義大利、葡萄牙也受到波及。與此同時，烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基周日(18日)指責川普試圖向基輔施壓，逼迫烏克蘭向俄羅斯投降。
歐元兌美元在今日早盤一度貶值0.5%，最低貶至 1.1183 美元，隨後部分收復跌幅，交投於 1.1212 美元附近。受歐元走弱拖累，東歐貨幣表現弱於其他新興市場貨幣，美元兌波蘭茲羅提升值0.5%，報3.9071；美元兌匈牙利福林走升0.5%，報324.88，美元兌保加利亞列弗亦升值0.5%，報1.7485。
澳洲聯邦銀行外匯策略師Carol Kong表示：「市場恐將持續為歐元計入風險溢價。歐元兌美元本周可能測試 1.1130支撐價位，尤其是在地緣緊張進一步推高美元的情況下。」
paras_en: Rising US‑Ukraine tensions and large‑scale protests in France have dented market confidence in the euro, causing the euro to fall against most G10 currencies during Asian early‑trade on the 19th.

Over the weekend, protests in several French cities escalated into clashes between police and demonstrators, sparking the most severe street violence France has seen in years, including robberies and arson of landmark buildings. Demonstrations spread across multiple European countries, with France seeing the largest protests, and Belgium, Italy and Portugal also affected. At the same time, Ukrainian President Zelensky on Sunday (the 18th) accused former U.S. President Trump of trying to pressure Kyiv into surrendering to Russia.

The euro‑dollar pair slipped as much as 0.5% in early trade today, hitting a low of 1.1183 USD before partially regaining ground and trading around 1.1212 USD. The euro’s weakness also weighed on Eastern European currencies, which underperformed other emerging‑market currencies: the dollar rose 0.5% against the Polish zloty to 3.9071, against the Hungarian forint to 324.88, and against the Bulgarian lev to 1.7485.

Carol Kong, FX strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said: “The market is likely to continue pricing a risk premium into the euro. The euro‑dollar pair could test the 1.1130 support level this week, especially if geopolitical tensions further lift the dollar.”

items.title: 阿拉伯半島周遭海域周末頻傳商船遇襲！伊朗警告：美若恢復攻擊  已有「新作戰計畫」
items.title_en: Commercial Ships Frequently Attacked Around the Arabian Peninsula Over the Weekend; Iran Warns of a New Operational Plan if the U.S. Resumes Attacks
paras: 伊朗最高國家安全委員會秘書雷札伊周日(18日)警告，已針對美國與以色列「任何新的冒險行徑」擬定回應方案，並稱伊朗武裝力量的反制將比先前「12天戰爭」與「40天戰爭」更具毀滅性，「新作戰計畫不會遵循他們熟悉的規則」。
雷札伊身分相當具分量，曾任革命衛隊總司令，現掌伊朗安全決策核心機構。這一表態正值中東海域風險上升，因根據英國海上貿易行動辦公室數據，沙烏地阿拉伯朱拜勒附近海域接連有油輪遭不明發射物及火箭彈襲擊，阿曼灣、荷姆茲海峽週邊亦傳船舶受襲，船員暫報安全。
華府則同步釋放矛盾訊號。川普上周受訪時表示，不打算對伊朗使用核武器，也不預見部署美軍地面部隊，但華府仍保留常規打擊選項。
伊朗外長阿拉格齊則回應，德黑蘭不會在壓力下放棄主權權利，但仍準備對話。
分析人士認為，伊朗意在以強硬威懾換取談判籌碼，商船遇襲與荷姆茲通航風險則持續牽動能源市場神經。
paras_en: Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary, Rezaei, warned on Sunday (the 18th) that a response plan has been drafted for any new adventurism by the United States and Israel, and said Iran’s armed forces would retaliate with a level of devastation greater than the previous “12‑day war” and “40‑day war,” noting that the new operational plan would not follow the rules they are accustomed to.

Rezaei’s statement carries weight; he is a former commander of the Revolutionary Guard and now heads Iran’s core security‑decision body. The remark comes as risks in Middle‑East waters rise, with UK Maritime Trade Operations data showing a series of attacks on tankers near Saudi Arabia’s Jabal al‑Dukhan, as well as incidents in the Oman Sea and the Strait of Hormuz where vessels were struck by unknown projectiles and rockets, though crews have so far reported being safe.

Washington simultaneously sent mixed signals. In an interview last week, President Trump said he does not intend to use nuclear weapons against Iran and does not foresee deploying U.S. ground troops, yet the administration still retains the option of conventional strikes.
Iranian Foreign Minister Amir‑Abdollahian responded that Tehran will not relinquish its sovereign rights under pressure, but remains ready for dialogue.

Analysts believe Iran is using a hard‑line deterrent to gain bargaining chips in negotiations, and the ongoing attacks on commercial vessels and the navigation risk in the Strait of Hormuz continue to nerve the energy markets.

items.title_en: <New York Forex> US Dollar Records First Weekly Decline in Over a Month as Rate‑Hike Expectations Cool and AI Concerns Persist
paras: 美元周五(16日)走低，兌歐元與日元均創下逾1個月來首見單週貶值，反映市場對聯準會(Fed)升息的預期降溫，以及投資人對AI引發股市賣壓的疑慮持續存在。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.17%，報101.87，本週下跌約0.35%。
本週公布的消費者物價與生產者物價數據均高於預期，一度令市場感到不安。不過，聯準會官員的談話顯示，目前沒有急於進一步緊縮貨幣政策的必要，有助於穩定美國公債殖利率，也削弱了美元的支撐力道。
AI類股本週大幅下跌，壓力也蔓延至部分信用市場。由於投資人已大量押注AI供應鏈各個環節，如今開始擔心資料中心營運商可能無法及時實現獲利，進而償還債務。
StoneX全球市場研究主管Matt Weller表示，「我認為今天乃至本週最值得關注的現象，是美元與AI交易之間的緊密連動。通常科技股遭到拋售時，市場會預期美元因避險需求而走強。我們確實看到部分資金流向債券，但美元實際上卻在下跌。」
本週英鎊與瑞士法郎兌美元的升幅居前。瑞士法郎受到避險需求支撐，市場也預期，即使利率環境進一步走低，瑞士仍不太可能將政策利率降至目前零利率以下。
英鎊兌美元上漲0.31%，至1英鎊兌1.3314美元，本週累計上漲0.63%。
美元兌瑞士法郎則下跌0.25%，至0.8246瑞郎，本週累計下跌0.67%。瑞郎在過去兩個交易日累計升值逾1.4%。
芝商所（CME）FedWatch工具顯示，市場預估聯準會本月稍晚維持利率不變的機率為83%，高於一個月前的49%。
聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)週五出席在曼谷舉行的國際貨幣基金（IMF）與世界銀行年度會議時，並未透露未來利率決策的線索。他表示，自己不會「預先判斷」任何一次會議的決策。
紐約梅隆銀行宏觀經濟策略師John Velis表示，「我認為，目前聯準會決策委員會內部，尤其是理事們，尚未形成足夠共識支持10月升息。不過，12月是否升息仍是未解之題，從現在到那時還有許多事情可能發生。」
歐元區財政風險仍受關注
法國財政風險仍是市場關注的背景因素。10月初，法國債務風險溢價曾大幅攀升。
歐元兌美元上漲0.08%，至1歐元兌1.1227美元。歐元週四已上漲0.56%，創下兩個月來最大單日漲幅，全週上漲約0.23%。
投資人預期，美國總統川普將避免讓中東或烏克蘭局勢進一步升級，因為更大規模的衝突可能推升通膨，進而損害他在期中選舉前的政治支持度。
美元兌日元下跌0.08%，至158.11日元。日元終止連續四週貶值走勢，本週升值0.13%。此前，伊朗衝突支撐美元走強。
近期油價上漲推升美元，同時對歐元與日元等能源進口國貨幣造成壓力。
日本銀行（BOJ）總裁植田和男(Kazuo Ueda)週五再次強調，潛在通膨率可能超越央行設定的2%目標，仍是需要留意的風險。

paras_en: The dollar fell on Friday (the 16th), with both the euro and the yen posting their first weekly depreciation in more than a month, reflecting a cooling of market expectations for further Fed rate hikes and lingering investor worries that AI is weighing on equity markets.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.17% to 101.87, down about 0.35% for the week.

Consumer price and producer price data released this week came in above expectations, briefly unsettling markets. However, comments from Fed officials indicated no urgent need for further monetary tightening, helping to stabilise US Treasury yields and weakening support for the dollar.

AI‑related stocks fell sharply this week, and the pressure spread to parts of the credit market. Investors, who have heavily bet on every link of the AI supply chain, are now worried that data‑center operators may not generate profits quickly enough to service their debt.

Matt Weller, head of global market research at StoneX, said, "I think the most noteworthy phenomenon today and this week is the tight link between the dollar and AI trading. Usually when tech stocks are sold off, the market expects the dollar to strengthen on safe‑haven demand. We did see some flows into bonds, but the dollar actually fell."

The pound and the Swiss franc posted the biggest gains against the dollar this week. The franc was supported by safe‑haven demand, and markets expect that even if rates fall further, Switzerland is unlikely to push its policy rate below the current zero‑percent level.
The pound rose 0.31% to $1.3314, up 0.63% for the week.
The dollar slipped 0.25% against the Swiss franc to 0.8246 CHF, down 0.67% for the week. The franc had appreciated more than 1.4% over the past two trading days.
CME’s FedWatch tool shows the market now assigns an 83% probability that the Fed will keep rates unchanged later this month, up from 49% a month ago.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh attended the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday and offered no clues about future rate decisions, saying he does not "pre‑judge" the outcome of any meeting.

John Velis, macro strategy strategist at BNY Mellon, said, "I think the Fed’s policy committee, especially the governors, have not yet reached sufficient consensus to support a rate hike in October. However, whether there will be a hike in December remains an open question, and many things could happen between now and then."
Euro‑area fiscal risks remain a focus.
Fiscal risk in France continues to be a background concern for markets, with French sovereign risk premiums spiking sharply in early October.
The euro rose 0.08% to $1.1227. It had gained 0.56% on Thursday, the biggest single‑day rise in two months, and is up about 0.23% for the week.

Investors expect that President Trump will try to avoid further escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a larger conflict could push inflation higher and damage his political support ahead of the mid‑term elections.
The dollar fell 0.08% to ¥158.11, ending a four‑week streak of depreciation for the yen, which rose 0.13% this week. Previously, the Iran conflict had supported a stronger dollar.
Recent oil price gains have lifted the dollar while putting pressure on currencies of energy‑importing countries such as the euro and yen.
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated on Friday that a potential inflation rate above the BOJ’s 2% target remains a risk to watch.

items.title: 〈台幣〉股匯不同調 續貶7.3分失守32.3元關卡
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Weakens While Stocks Hold, Falling 0.73 ¢ to Slip Below the 32.3 TWD Mark
paras: 在美元指數維持強勢、外資持續撤出亞洲市場影響下，新台幣兌美元今 (16) 日走弱，終場收在32.338元，貶值7.3分，續創近期波段低點，顯示國際資金仍偏向美元資產，相較於昨天的91億美元爆巨量，台北外匯經紀公司與元太外匯經紀公司合計總成交量為 46.12億美元。
儘管匯市承壓，台股表現相對有撐，加權指數終場收在47,111點，上漲141點，漲幅約0.3%，呈現匯弱股強格局。市場買盤主要聚焦 AI 伺服器、高階 PCB 及半導體供應鏈族群，在電子權值股支撐下，大盤成功守住漲勢。
從籌碼面來看，統計今日三大法人合計賣超約729億元，其中外資賣超高達494億元，已連續第8個交易日站在賣方；投信則持續扮演護盤角色，買超約132億元，寫下連6買；自營商賣超約367億元。
市場人士指出，本波新台幣轉弱主要受到美元升值效應帶動，近期美國經濟數據維持韌性，加上市場重新評估聯準會後續政策路徑，推升美元買盤，亞洲主要貨幣同步承壓，新台幣也不例外。資料顯示，10月以來新台幣已由31字頭一路走貶至32.3元以上水準。
觀察資金流向，外資近期持續調節台股權值股與電子類股部位，成為匯市與股市的重要變數。不過投信買盤明顯進場承接，加上AI相關產業基本面未見轉弱，因此支撐台股維持高檔震盪格局。今天市場呈現「匯率偏空、股市偏多」，除外資匯出導致台幣走弱，加上AI、高效能運算(HPC)及先進封裝需求仍強，吸引國內資金與長線買盤進駐，使台股維持相對強勢。
paras_en: Under a strong US dollar index and continued foreign‑capital outflows from Asian markets, the New Taiwan dollar weakened against the US dollar today (Oct 16), closing at 32.338 TWD, down 0.73 ¢ and extending its recent low‑point swing, indicating that international funds remain biased toward dollar assets. In contrast to yesterday’s massive USD 91 billion turnover, Taipei’s foreign‑exchange brokers and Yuan‑Tai FX brokers together handled a total volume of USD 46.12 billion.

Despite pressure on the currency market, Taiwan’s equity market showed relative resilience, with the weighted index closing at 47,111 points, up 141 points or about 0.3%, reflecting a “weak currency, strong stocks” pattern. Buying interest centered on AI servers, high‑end PCBs and semiconductor supply‑chain groups, and the rally in heavyweight electronics stocks helped the market maintain its upward momentum.

From a flow perspective, the three major institutional investors sold a combined net NT$729 billion today, with foreign investors leading the sell‑side at NT$494 billion for the eighth consecutive trading day. Trust funds continued to play a stabilising role, net‑buying about NT$132 billion for the sixth straight session, while proprietary traders sold roughly NT$367 billion.

Market observers said the recent weakening of the Taiwan dollar is mainly driven by the dollar’s appreciation. Recent US economic data remain resilient and the market’s reassessment of the Fed’s policy path has boosted dollar demand, putting pressure on major Asian currencies, including the TWD. Data show that since October the Taiwan dollar has slid from the low‑31s to above the 32.3 TWD level.

Looking at capital flows, foreign investors have been adjusting their positions in Taiwan’s heavyweight and electronics stocks, becoming a key variable for both the FX and equity markets. However, trust‑fund buying is evident, and the fundamentals of AI‑related industries have not weakened, supporting the Taiwan stock market’s high‑level range‑bound pattern. Today’s market displayed a “bearish currency, bullish equity” stance: foreign outflows weakened the TWD, while strong demand for AI, high‑performance computing and advanced packaging kept domestic and long‑term buying interest in equities, allowing the stock market to stay relatively strong.

胡塞武裝和伊朗加大襲擊沙烏地阿拉伯及途經荷姆茲海峽船隻，引發汽油價格飆升，影響美國9月消費者價格漲幅加快，同時美國聯邦準備理事會(FED)褐皮書顯示燃料成本上升加劇物價壓力，可能在11月3日期中選舉前再打擊美國總統川普及其所屬的共和黨，而且FED官員發表審慎言論，導致指標美國十年期公債收益率回落至三周低點，促使市場降低對FED在10月加息的押注，週四壓抑美元；此外，日本8月核心機械訂單分別較前月與上年同期增加5.2%和18.6%優於預期，並據日本央行(BOJ)審議委員小枝淳子表示，通貨膨脹存在相當大上行風險，BOJ在加息問題上不應過於謹慎，同時認為日本中性利率遠高於1%，表明BOJ政策利率仍有空間進一步上調，而且日本經濟財政大臣城內實稱，日本已告別通貨緊縮時代，將兼顧增長與財政紀律，提供日圓支撐，並隨著日本股市暴跌，引發資金湧向日本公債避險，更有日本出口商與投機客賣盤，衝擊美元兌日圓自158.33高點下挫。

paras: 美元周四(15日)自18個月高點回落，投資人將目光從強勁的美國通膨與消費支出數據，轉向 AI 資料中心業者債券遭拋售的情況。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌 0.45%，報 101.99。此前美國通膨數據高於預期，美元指數週三升至 18 個月高點。
美國 9 月生產者物價(PPI)以 4 年半來最快速度上漲，商品與服務成本同步增加，進一步顯示通膨壓力正從能源領域擴散至其他領域。
上個月零售銷售增幅高於預期，主要受到汽油價格上漲帶動，每週初領失業救濟金人數則小幅增加，顯示消費需求仍具韌性，勞動市場也維持穩定。
但美國公債價格上漲，美元則回落，反映聯準會(Fed)官員近期發表審慎言論，進一步降低市場對 10 月升息的預期。
Monex USA交易主管 Juan Perez 表示，「目前市場存在一種不利美元的論述，原因在於，通膨若維持在這樣的水準，且以如此快的速度上升，將難以持續。」
他表示，「無論戰事方面沒有好消息，或股市前景看起來悲觀，在過去四週美元大幅走強之後，市場仍傾向拋售美元……經濟停滯似乎對交易員的想法產生更大的影響。」
AI企業債務負擔受關注
美元回落帶動歐元反彈，歐元兌美元上漲 0.56%，從 18 個月低點升至 1.1218 美元，創下近兩個月來最大單日漲幅。
英鎊兌美元則上漲 0.64%，至 1.3275 美元，此前數據顯示，英國經濟 8 月意外成長 0.1%。
週三美國消費者物價指數（CPI）數據高於預期，最初推升市場對聯準會維持高利率更長時間的押注。同時，市場再度擔憂 AI 企業沉重的債務負擔，促使資金流向美國公債等避險資產，市場走勢因而震盪加劇。
Mesirow Currency Management 資深投資策略師 Uto Shinohara 表示，「晶片股遭拋售為債券提供支撐，使殖利率得以維持在相對受控的水準，抵銷通膨訊號帶來的影響。」
芝商所（CME Group）FedWatch 工具顯示，交易員目前預期，聯準會在 10 月 27 日至 28 日的會議上維持利率不變的機率為 73%，高於一個月前的 53%。
CPI 報告公布後，市場對升息的預期機率大幅上升，但聯準會負責監管事務的副主席鮑曼 (Michelle Bowman)，以及舊金山聯準銀行總裁戴莉 (Mary Daly) 等官員表示，聯準會可以等到會議前取得更明確的資訊再做決定，隨後市場對升息的押注便有所降溫。
LMAX Group 市場策略師 Joel Kruger 表示，「如果殖利率難以進一步走高，而美元每逢反彈便持續遭到賣出，將會強化我們的看法：通膨消息大致已被市場消化，風險的整體平衡將有利於風險性資產。」
投資人週五也將關注聯準會官員在曼谷舉行的國際貨幣基金（IMF）與世界銀行年度會議上的談話，包括聯準會主席華許 (Kevin Warsh)，以尋找美國央行下一步行動的線索。

日元則升值 0.15%，至每美元兌 158.08 日元。
Shinohara 表示，「聯準會即將進入政策會議前的靜默期，而會議前也不再有一級重要經濟數據公布，因此市場走勢可能仍將受到俄羅斯與烏克蘭、伊朗相關地緣政治不確定性，以及 AI 產業發展的影響。」

paras_en: The dollar fell on Thursday (the 15th) from an 18‑month high as investors shifted their focus from strong U.S. inflation and consumer spending data to the sell‑off in bonds of AI data‑center operators.

In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.45% to 101.99. Earlier, U.S. inflation data came in above expectations, pushing the index to an 18‑month peak on Wednesday.

U.S. September producer prices (PPI) rose at the fastest pace in four and a half years, with costs for goods and services climbing together, further showing inflation pressure spreading from the energy sector to other areas.

Last month’s retail sales growth exceeded expectations, driven mainly by higher gasoline prices, while initial unemployment claims rose slightly, indicating consumer demand remains resilient and the labor market stays stable.
However, U.S. Treasury prices rose and the dollar retreated, reflecting recent cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials that further lowered market expectations of a rate hike in October.

Juan Perez, head of trading at Monex USA, said, "There is currently a narrative that is unfavorable to the dollar because if inflation stays at this level and rises this quickly, it will be hard to sustain."

He added, "Whether there is no good news on the war front or the equity outlook looks bleak, after the dollar’s strong run over the past four weeks the market still tends to sell the greenback… stagnation seems to have a bigger impact on traders’ thinking."
AI companies' debt burdens draw attention
The dollar’s decline lifted the euro, which rose 0.56% against the dollar from an 18‑month low to $1.1218, marking the biggest single‑day gain in nearly two months.
The pound rose 0.64% to $1.3275 after data showed the U.K. economy unexpectedly grew 0.1% in August.

Wednesday’s U.S. consumer price index (CPI) came in above expectations, initially boosting bets that the Fed would keep rates high for longer. At the same time, renewed worries about heavy debt loads at AI firms prompted a flow into safe‑haven assets such as U.S. Treasuries, intensifying market volatility.

Uto Shinohara, senior investment strategist at Mesirow Currency Management, said, "The sell‑off in chip stocks provided support for bonds, keeping yields at relatively controlled levels and offsetting the impact of inflation signals."
The CME Group FedWatch tool shows traders now assign a 73% probability that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its Oct. 27‑28 meeting, up from 53% a month ago.

After the CPI report, the market’s probability of a rate hike surged, but Fed Vice‑Chair Michelle Bowman and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said the Fed could wait for clearer information before deciding, cooling the market’s rate‑hike bets.

LMAX Group market strategist Joel Kruger said, "If yields struggle to rise further and the dollar keeps getting sold each time it rebounds, it reinforces our view that inflation news has largely been priced in and the overall risk balance will favor risky assets."
Investors will also watch Friday for comments from Fed officials at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, including Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, for clues on the central bank’s next move.
The Australian dollar fell 0.77% to $0.6919 after September job numbers in Australia unexpectedly dropped.
The yen appreciated 0.15% to 158.08 per dollar.

Shinohara noted, "The Fed is entering a pre‑meeting quiet period, and no major economic data will be released before the meeting, so market moves may still be influenced by geopolitical uncertainties related to Russia, Ukraine, Iran, and the development of the AI industry."
